subtopics.title: From First Villages to an Urban World

questions.question: The formula for the birth of towns is:
options: Mining plus railways equals a town
Surplus plus specialisation plus exchange equals a town
Defence plus religion equals a town
Factories plus harbours equals a town

questions.question: The first true urban settlements grew in:
options: River valleys such as the Nile and Tigris-Euphrates

questions.question: Compared with developed countries, developing countries today generally have:
options: A lower level of urbanisation but a faster rate
A higher level of urbanisation and a slower rate
Both a higher level and a slower rate

questions.question: Urbanisation is defined as an increase in:
options: The number of buildings in a city
The physical size of the built-up area
The number of people in cities
The percentage of a population living in urban areas

questions.question: Cities gain people while the urban percentage stays constant. This is:
Urban sprawl differs from urban expansion because sprawl is:
options: Any outward growth of a city
Low-density, unplanned or poorly planned outward spread

questions.question: Retirees and remote workers moving from Johannesburg to small Western Cape coastal towns illustrate:

subtopics.title: Site, Situation and the Functional Classification of Towns

questions.question: Johannesburg's location shows that:
options: A good enough situation can overrule a poor site
A good site always beats situation
Gold is a site factor only

questions.question: The region served by a central place is called its:
Durban is the textbook South African break-of-bulk point because:
options: It sits at a mountain pass
Cargo transfers there between ship, rail and road, attracting processing industry

questions.question: Which pairing of town and functional type is correct?
options: Worcester — gap town at a Cape Fold Mountains pass

subtopics.title: Urban Hierarchy and Land-Use Zones: The Anatomy of a City

questions.question: The see-saw rule of the urban hierarchy states that:
options: All settlements offer the same services
High-order services are found in every village
Many small places offer low-order services; few large places offer high-order services

questions.question: The CBD's signature combination is:
options: Highest land values, tallest buildings, greatest accessibility
Cheapest land, low buildings, poor transport

questions.question: The transition zone around the CBD is characterised by:
options: Mixed, changing land use — subdivided old buildings, light industry, decay beside renewal

questions.question: Apartheid planning deformed the residential pattern of SA cities by:
options: Placing townships next to the CBD
Placing townships on the far urban edge, separated by buffer strips, railways and industry
Building all housing at equal density

subtopics.title: Why Cities Exist and Why Everyone Is Moving to Them

questions.question: In the simplified story, the "whole secret" that first made towns possible was:
Factories accelerated urban growth because they are:
options: Gathering machines that pull thousands of workers to one gate

questions.question: In the parked-car picture, a developed country's urbanisation is like a car that is:
options: Out of fuel at the bottom
Already parked at the top of the hill — high level, slow rate

subtopics.title: The Ladder of Shops and the Jobs Towns Do

questions.question: In the shopping-trip picture, bread and airtime from the corner spaza represent:
options: Low-order goods offered by many small, nearby places

questions.question: The "shop-keeper town" serving surrounding farms and villages is a:
"Towns forgive a bad site for a good enough reason" refers to:
options: Johannesburg growing on Witwatersrand gold despite a poor site

questions.question: Which one-line job description is correctly matched?
options: Musina — holds a door between countries as a gateway town

subtopics.title: A Taxi Ride Across the Zones

questions.question: CBD buildings grow tall because:
options: Land is so expensive that floor space must be stacked to afford it
The CBD has the most residents

questions.question: The zone described as "half building site, half waiting room" is the:
Heavy industry stretches along railways and highways because it needs:
options: Flat land and bulk transport, away from high-value housing

questions.question: Sandton, Gateway and Century City are examples of:
options: Decentralised nodes pulling CBD functions toward highways and high-income suburbs
